reviewer.baseline: provisional; not host activation or accepted release evidence

disposition: Two P2 caller-boundary findings, plus explicit host invalidation/activation requirements. Focused synthetic caller behavior reproduced; Morgan owns final verdict and any integration.

findings.title: Sparse receipt file arrays skip all selected-file validation
findings.trigger: Injected trusted loader returns a real valid corpus with receipt.files=new Array(1) for a one-file descriptor. Array.isArray and length checks pass; Array.some skips the empty slot.
findings.impact: Caller accepts a malformed receipt containing no selected-file row, renders one resource and returns that receipt. This breaks the explicit receipt match/traceability boundary. The reproduction still used the real pinned synthetic loader/corpus; no incorrect release, production exposure or malicious capability bypass is claimed. The selected transport itself returns dense receipts; this targets the generic caller result guard.

findings.repairRecommendation: Validate each numeric receipt index explicitly (including own slot presence and non-null object shape) before accessing key/hash/bytes/indexes, or normalize to a dense sequence and reject missing rows. Keep exact file count/order/pin comparisons. Add a sparse-array negative alongside null/undefined rows.
findings.source: New caller guard introduced in this delta.

findings.title: Mutable admission object hides a policy-ID change during loading
findings.trigger: Trusted authorize() returns its shared mutable policy object instead of a clone. During actual load, policy.policyId changes. The first admission.permission aliases the same object returned by the second authorization.
findings.impact: Both sides of the intended policy-ID stability check now read changed-policy, so loading/rendering succeeds despite policy identity changing. Equivalent cloned decisions correctly reject. This is a correctness defect in the promised stable admission comparison, not evidence that descriptor claims bypass authorization: both real callback decisions remained allowed and account/scope unchanged in this repro.

findings.repairRecommendation: Snapshot the admission policy ID and all compared grant/account/scope fields into independent validated values immediately after authorization. Compare the second decision against that snapshot, not a provider-owned mutable object. Add shared-object and cloned-object policy change regression cases; retain the current owner/scope/selection checks.

capabilityAndBindingAssessment.descriptorVersusCapability: selectedCommonPackage is data. Availability of load alone or descriptor.permission allowed claims is refused; authorize must be an independently trusted host capability. Test policy is separately retained, synthetic and not a real producer admission.
capabilityAndBindingAssessment.schemaAndContract: Caller checks schema/contract SHA256 syntax and includes qualification pins in canonical selection attested by independent authorize. It does not fetch/hash schema or contract bytes, and loader options omit qualification. Authentic producer schema/contract approval must therefore be established inside the trusted authorization capability; synthetic fixture hashes are not that proof.
capabilityAndBindingAssessment.releaseManifestFiles: Exact release ID/accepted release + manifest URL/hash + file order/key/hash/compressed bytes/packet indexes compared at caller, with F1 dense-row exception. The selected transport SHA bytes match 77eb80d0e91fd3b10e42d2df83fd71c70713564b and independently validates synthetic package/contract version, streamed gzip bytes and structural schema.
capabilityAndBindingAssessment.accountAndScope: Explicit guest/demo/user:<id> namespace, authorizer account match, matching privateOwnerId, public-only user scope and allowLocalRestricted=false. Descriptor readerOptions privileges are ignored. Current scope change is detected even when policy object is shared because primitive reader options were captured.
capabilityAndBindingAssessment.rightsRecheck: Initial authorization then another after load, before first reader installation/render. Denial, selection change, account mismatch and cloned policy change fail; F2 mutable alias defeats policy-ID change check.
capabilityAndBindingAssessment.staleLoading: Focused tests pass account/reset cancellation, no-reset account check after awaited work, pending authorization cancellation, newer load and stale completion, local-file interruption and abort-ignoring capability completion. No stale in-flight render observed in those checks.
capabilityAndBindingAssessment.immutablePresentation: Focused checks preserve descriptor, original Arabic source/fingerprint, English translation/citations, IRI/expression text and source URLs; unresolved joins retained. Read-only save/export and preview locale changes cause no persistence/provider/session effects.
capabilityAndBindingAssessment.io: Setup performs no automatic package I/O. Explicit load invokes only trusted injected test fetch; no automatic discovery or dependency chase, ambient/provider calls, save/export/profile persistence. Direct invocation of disabled controls remains guarded.

hostAndCacheGaps.actualHost: public/app.js:180 invokes setupData without selectedCommonPackage/commonPackageLoader; no host action invokes loadSelectedCommonPackage. Feature entry activation, real descriptor/capability provisioning and real-release/browser/live hosting qualification are absent.
hostAndCacheGaps.existingIdentityHook: public/app.js:75 switchAccount calls dataUi.reset(), which clears cached reader/global resolver. This hook must be retained in any host activation.
hostAndCacheGaps.cachedAccountProbe: After completed Alice-private load, switching getter to Bob without host reset and triggering locale render retains two rows and Alice private resolver. Calling ui.reset first clears rows/resolver. This is host-lifecycle dependence, not a demonstrated production leak: actual host already calls reset and package loading is unactivated.
hostAndCacheGaps.cachedPolicyProbe: Policy allowed=false after a successful public load followed by locale render does not call authorize again; two original calls remain, translation still renders. No same-account policy-invalidation signal is wired. Declare whether load-time authorization is a session snapshot or add invalidation/recheck before cached render if rights must remain current. Treat this as an activation requirement, not passing rights-revocation evidence.

preservation.noRuntimeServersOrNetwork: Focused Node tests with synthetic gzip + injected fetch and minimal DOM only; ambient network forbidden by fixture. No browser/runtime qualification.

boundedSourceSnapshot: 17 selected tracked code/test/package metadata files, 176670 bytes; no corpus/dependency copies. Recursive relative imports only; source digests and caller delta hash verified. No installs, Git-writing fixtures, worktrees, extra agents/workers/sessions, servers or external writes.
controls: Supplied filesystem/network retained; mandatory reviewer auto_review. Separate approval policy unavailable; no named profile inferred from unset environment. Git subprocesses remove inherited GIT_* and use explicit no-config/no-prompt/no-optional-lock policy.
limitations: All caller presentation checks use minimal DOM stubs and trusted injected synthetic byte transport; no native browser, actual secure-context/CORS/HTTP Content-Encoding or production hosting qualification.

Trusted authorize/load capabilities are an external authority boundary. The caller cannot prove an injected authorizer did genuine producer rights/schema/contract qualification merely from its attestation.
Review does not repeat producer/transport full suite, access actual retained corpus partitions or admit any real source/release.
Both P2 findings target generic caller guard behavior and do not show an attack by untrusted descriptor data against an independently correct capability.
Local report/snapshots are untracked reviewer artifacts; source HEAD/branches/indexes and prior recall artifacts unchanged.
recommendedMorganNextStep: Repair F1/F2 and recheck these exact edge cases. Before host activation, obtain independent producer admission/capability binding and explicit account/policy cache invalidation behavior, then qualify browser/live hosting/real-release paths separately.
